results.title: Data driven design for urban street shading: Validation and application of ladybug tools as a design tool for outdoor thermal comfort - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Data driven design for urban street shading: Validation and application of ladybug tools as a design tool for outdoor thermal comfort. The value of data-driven shade design for thermal comfort is highlighted. Integrating microclimate simulation into design workflows can optimize shade design by considering all thermal effects. This paper validates two workflows using Ladybug Tools (LBT) for modelling freestanding shade, proposing their design applicability. A novel workflow models shortwave and longwave effects of lightweight shade materials on outdoor thermal comfort, differing from LBT's standard approach by considering shade interactions in longwave radiation exchanges. Simulated mean radiant temperature (MRT) is validated against field measurements and compared across both workflows. The custom workflow is applied to a design case study in Turin, Italy, evaluating various shade materials and their effects on MRT. Results demonstrate how shade material, height, ground material, and time of day interact to influence cooling effects, emphasizing practical implications for optimizing shade design.

results.title: Natural shading vs. artificial shading: A comparative analysis of their cooling efficacy in extreme hot weather - ScienceDirect
results.content: This study offers valuable insights for urban designers to create sustainable shaded communities and also initiates a discourse for revising local heat warning systems, considering various thermal stress indices. According to the evidence in the literature, tree shading can alleviate heat stress and improve the microclimate, and the cooling potentials differ by tree species (de Abreu-Harbich et al., 2015), canopy characteristics (Chen et al., 2019), planting configuration (Chen et al., 2021), and climate backgrounds (Helletsgruber et al., 2020). Over 165 thermal indices are documented in the current literature (de Freitas and Grigorieva, 2017), encompassing those specially developed for hot conditions, like Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT), Heat Index (HI); as well as those adapted for outdoor environment, such as Predicted Mean Vote (PMV), Physiological Equivalent Temperature (PET), and Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI). According to previous studies, these four indices have been used in outdoor spaces (i.e., open space, semi-open space, and shaded areas) in hot and humid climates (Huang et al., 2016; Li et al., 2023a, Li et al., 2023b; Manavvi and Rajasekar, 2022). Therefore, this study is to compare the relative cooling efficacy of natural and artificial shading on outdoor microclimate and thermal stress conditions. The microclimate and thermal stress performance of three types of outdoor environments, namely open space, artificial shading, and natural shading, were compared in Fig. 5. This study systematically compared two types of natural and artificial covering, providing valuable empirical evidence for the comparative cooling efficacy of different shading solutions in urban environments, especially for extremely hot conditions (Cheung and Jim, 2018a; Colter et al., 2019). In the context of creating a sustainable community with robust climate adaptation, this study aimed to compare the efficacy of outdoor microclimate and thermal stress between two types of shading solutions: natural canopies and artificial coverings. * ### Analyzing the cooling effect, thermal comfort, and energy consumption of integrated arrangement of high-rise buildings and green spaces on urban heat island. Street shade, a typical cooling shelter for urban dwellers, has been primarily investigated for outdoor thermal comfort but not extensively under extreme heat conditions. This study explores the cooling efficacy of diverse street shade types in mitigating urban heat, thereby facilitating cities and their residents' adaptation to climatic shifts.

results.content: # Review of the Role of Urban Green Infrastructure on Climate Resiliency: A Focus on Heat Mitigation Modelling Scenario on the Microclimate and Building Scale. This systematic review explores the role of urban green infrastructure (UGI) in enhancing climate resilience, focusing mainly on heat mitigation modelling and its application at both urban and building scales. urban green infrastructure; climate resilience; heat mitigation; simulation models; future climate scenarios. The aim was to analyse the latest knowledge of UGI modelling tools, techniques, simulation scenarios and results in the context of urban and building scales for heat mitigation. results.title: Climate adaptation in informal areas in hot arid climates - Lotfata - 2024 - Sustainable Development - Wiley Online Library
results.content: This conceptual and exploratory research study investigates, systematically and holistically, climate-adaptive spatial design interventions for high-density informal urban areas in hot arid climates, which remain understudied despite their vulnerability to heat stress and the heat-vulnerable groups populating them. Five streetscape design prototypes are proposed that include climate-adaptive spatial interventions appraised qualitatively with consideration to relevant feasibility matters: land use planning, equity, affordability, mobility, and sense of place. The study shows that there is potential for climate-adaptive interventions in informal urban areas in hot arid climates, but that these interventions also present challenges. However, the study of climate-adaptive design for high-density informal urban areas in hot arid climates remains limited and poses unique challenges due to the combination of a harsh climate type and the limited availability of regulatory instruments and financial means to adapt to climate change. Fueled by these concerns, this study addresses the question: what climate-adaptive spatial design interventions are most feasible in high-density informal urban areas in hot arid climates? This qualitative, interdisciplinary research study investigates systematically and holistically, with research through design (RTD), feasible climate-adaptive spatial design interventions in high-density informal urban areas in hot arid climates. An informal neighborhood in the Shubra district, Cairo, is used as a study case to develop prototypical climate-adaptive spatial interventions potentially replicable across informal urban areas in Cairo, and other cities in hot arid climates. The interventions found in step 1 were categorized into three groups of climate-adaptive design strategies (Table 1): adapting urban materials (increasing albedo values and/or changing specific heat properties of surfacing materials), implementing shade (blocking direct solar radiation by implementing artificial shading structures), and introducing vegetation (provision of cooling through shading and evapotranspiration). The process described in the previous section resulted in five design prototypes for climate-adaptive streetscapes in informal urban areas in hot arid climates (P4) that include climate-adaptiveness, land use planning, equity, affordability, mobility, and sense of place criteria. This is a conceptual and exploratory interdisciplinary research study that investigates feasible climate-adaptive spatial design interventions in high-density informal urban areas in hot arid climates from a multidisciplinary perspective.
